messages:
sofia: heads up — getting reports from a midmarket customer hitting intermittent 429s for streaming endpoints while chat+embeddings stay healthy. they can reproduce with long-lived SSE streams. :eyes:

mike: is the 429 coming from our edge (gateway) or from the runtime pools? any headers in the responses?

sofia: gateway 429 with Retry-After but no X-RateLimit-* headers. runtime logs show the request made it to the pod, then dropped on quota check.

anika: that sounds like a policy mismatch between per-key global bucket and endpoint-specific enforcement. streaming is still counted as "requests" in the gateway but runtime expects token-based accounting for streaming frames.

lee: streaming is tricky — we charge/limit by concurrent stream handles + tokens/second once the stream is active. If gateway only enforces request/sec, you get weird bursts on open streams.

sofia: customer reported they ramp quickly (50 new streams in <30s) and then get 429s on the stream open call, but after 90s things smooth out.

mike: could be burst window: gateway has a small token-bucket with capacity 100 for per-key bursts. but runtime is enforcing a per-org in-flight limit that is lower. mismatch = gateway allows open, runtime rejects when checking active_handles.

anika: proposal: enforce per-key_and_endpoint token buckets at the gateway with knobs: capacity, refill_rate, and an optional concurrent_handles limit for streaming endpoints. that gives consistent 429s with proper headers.

product-ux: from a console UX perspective we need to expose per-endpoint quotas (chat/embeddings/rerank/streaming) and a burst slider (0-500 tokens or handles) and a toggle for "allow bursts beyond committed quota". also show a live sample of X-RateLimit-* headers the client will see.

sarah: agree. also telemetry: we should emit metrics: quota.allow, quota.deny, quota.burst_used, per_endpoint_inflight, and histogram of retry-after to drive dashboard graphs.

lee: implementation detail: two-layer model — fast-path gateway pre-check (cheap counters) and authoritative runtime check. both must reference same config store. current bug: gateway reads env config while runtime reads config service — drift during rollouts.

mike: we should add an integration test that simulates 200 concurrent stream opens and verifies deterministic 429 rate and header set. plus a chaos test where config rollouts happen mid-ramp.

sofia: small config example for discussion:
```json
{
  "quota_rules": {
    "default": {"rate_per_sec": 50, "burst_capacity": 100},
    "endpoints": {
      "chat": {"rate_per_sec": 40, "burst_capacity": 80, "accounting": "tokens"},
      "embeddings": {"rate_per_sec": 10, "burst_capacity": 20, "accounting": "requests"},
      "rerank": {"rate_per_sec": 5, "burst_capacity": 10, "accounting": "requests"},
      "streaming": {"concurrent_handles": 20, "burst_handles": 40, "token_rate": 200}
    }
  }
}
```

anika: that looks reasonable. note: "streaming" needs both concurrency and sustained token throughput accounting. we should also add per-org overrides and per-key caps that can't exceed org cap.

product-ux: For console UI, show a stacked bar: committed vs burst vs used for each endpoint. admins should be able to edit per-org overrides and preview impact (simulated traffic).

ops-bot: FYI deploy queued: quota-config-sync v2 -> canary (10%) at 1748001800

mike: after canary, validate gateway+runtime read from the same config endpoint and add an assertion in the config rollout job to reject diffs where gateway/runtime keys mismatch.

sofia: also add clearer 429 body when reject is due to "concurrent_handles" vs "rate" so SDKs can distinguish and backoff properly. e.g., {"error":"rate_limit","reason":"concurrent_handles","retry_after":12}.

lee: telemetry note: emit quota.reason tag on span so we can filter traces where quota denied. saves us from digging through logs.

anika: ops checklist: 1) unify config source, 2) implement endpoint-specific gateway checks, 3) add per-endpoint headers, 4) update console UX, 5) add tests + canary.

sofia: assigning owners: mike for gateway checks + headers, anika for runtime enforcement update, product-ux for console changes, lee for telemetry/dashboard, sarah for tests.

deploy-bot: canary rolled out to 10% at 1748001800 :rocket:

mike: I'll start a small RFC doc and a follow-up PR. tagging @product-ux for wireframes.

product-ux: got it — will sketch and share tomorrow. :+1:

sofia: thanks folks. i'll follow up with the customer with timeline and workaround (set a slower client-side ramp and retry with exponential backoff). :thumbsup:
